critical_paths.property: Public getters and view functions (admissionStatus, canPurchase, denominationAmount, getActiveIds/Shapes, items, requiredReserve, restockFee, immutables) are pure reads: they mutate no storage and transfer no value, and their reads of trusted FWA/Shapes state feed the safety invariants.
critical_paths.attacker_control: A caller chooses the arguments and the calling context but cannot, through any view path, write pool storage or move ETH/NFTs; the external reads here go to the fixed, trusted FWA pool and Shapes contracts resolved at construction.
critical_paths.asset_authority_ledger: No wei or NFT changes custody on any view path; balance, profit, keeperCredit and curated custody are unchanged by a read. These getters only report the ledger that the money-moving paths (P3/P4/P5) maintain.
critical_paths.counterexample: A view returning a stale or manipulable value that a money path trusts without re-check, letting an attacker nudge a reported count to flip a branch; no such write-through-view was found and the stateful cycle reads these at rest and asserts the invariants hold.

postconditions.assertion: The view/getter surface performs no storage write and no value transfer; the stateful cycle reads these getters at rest after every step and the asserted invariants (profit<=balance, item count == sum(activeShapes)) hold.
postconditions.possible_false_positive: The invariant read could pass while a getter silently returns a value inconsistent with storage, because the test reads the same getter it trusts rather than an independent oracle.
postconditions.adversarial_variant: An attacker nudges admissionStatus/requiredReserve inputs (unsettled count, mint fee) so a downstream gate mis-fires while the getter still looks consistent; requiredReserve/admissionStatus read trusted FWA state and the below-reserve and stateful runs exercised those gates.

identity.reason: Getters expose immutables and creator/keeper identity; the authorization matrix confirms identity-gated writes are elsewhere, not on these reads.

quantity.reason: admissionStatus/requiredReserve compute counts and reserve from trusted FWA state; the stateful and below-reserve runs exercised those quantities at rest.

value_attribution.reason: No value is attributed or moved on a view path.

authorization.reason: Views are unauthenticated by design; the creator/keeper gates sit on the write paths validated in the security matrix.

callback.reason: External reads target the fixed trusted FWA/Shapes contracts; no attacker-controlled callback is reachable from a view.

timing.reason: Getter values can be read at any time but feed gates re-evaluated inside the money paths; timing of reads moves nothing.

critical_paths.attacker_control: A non-creator/non-keeper attacker calls each admin function and attempts a stale pool-page signature replay or an out-of-epoch digest; the attacker also controls the untracked-NFT contract passed to recoverUntrackedNFT and the ENS name string.
critical_paths.asset_authority_ledger: Authority over configuration, pool-page signing and creator role must stay with the creator; recoverUntrackedNFT may only move NFTs that are not tracked pool inventory, so tracked custody and ETH balances are untouched by these paths.
critical_paths.counterexample: A replayed or cross-epoch pool-page signature validating as ERC-1271, or recoverUntrackedNFT sweeping a tracked prize/curated NFT, or a clone initialized outside the factory escaping the implementation lock; the security matrix exercised each and all are gated.

postconditions.possible_false_positive: The matrix could assert a revert reason without reaching the state-changing body, so a gate that is present but mis-scoped would still look enforced.
postconditions.adversarial_variant: A keeper-only or creator-only function reachable by the other role, or by an arbitrary caller when the pool is in a particular lifecycle state; the matrix and keeper-scope tests exercised the lifecycle-gated cases.

postconditions.assertion: approvePoolPage records a digest valid under isValidSignature only within the current pageEpoch; a creator change or revokePoolPages bumps the epoch and invalidates prior digests (testPoolPageEpochReplay).
postconditions.possible_false_positive: The replay test could check a different digest than the one approved, so a replay that reuses the exact prior digest might pass unnoticed.
postconditions.adversarial_variant: Replaying an approved digest after a creator handover or revocation, or forging a digest for an unapproved page; the epoch-replay test approves, validates, rotates and re-checks the same digest.

quantity.reason: These admin paths move configuration and role, not quantities of pooled value.

value_attribution.reason: recoverUntrackedNFT is guarded to non-tracked NFTs only, so it cannot re-attribute tracked prize/curated custody.

critical_paths.property: Proceeds must split by the markup-derived profit share of the listing set the draws were priced on; a creator must not book more profit than the honest split while the fund is below the reserve (the 'game first' invariant).
critical_paths.attacker_control: The creator fully controls the listing set and its timing: it can withdrawCurated (or otherwise mutate activeIds) before collecting, choosing when to collect relative to keeper reconciliation, in the game-first regime (fund < reserve, reached via an unreconciled settled draw).
critical_paths.asset_authority_ledger: Curated NFT sale proceeds are fund money (curated share == 0) and must back the reserve while short; the invariant is that balance - profit (the fund) never drops because of a creator listing-set change before collection.
critical_paths.counterexample: Withdraw all curated NFTs, then collect: _collect splits all accrued proceeds by the current profitShareSum/activeIds.length, so removing zero-share curated listings raises the creator numerator and books fund money as withdrawable profit while the pool is underfunded; the fund ends strictly lower.

postconditions.assertion: withdrawCurated-then-collect books 0.001985->0.002383 ETH (factor n/(n-1)) on identical proceeds, while unlistShapes/listCurated/transfer/configure are neutral or fund-favourable; the lever scales as k/(n-k) for k curated of n listings.
postconditions.possible_false_positive: The extent test fixes one board and markup, so a passing per-action comparison could understate or overstate the lever on other boards where share(m) or k/(n-k) differ.
postconditions.adversarial_variant: An automatic (no creator action) curated draw booking NFT money as profit, or a larger multiplier via a different board; the worst-case test drives 10 curated of 20 at 100% markup to bound the net extraction.

postconditions.assertion: At launch worst case the honest collect books 0 profit (fund keeps 0.085 ETH) yet withdraw-all-then-collect books 0.01738 ETH withdrawable profit and the fund drops to 0.0677 ETH: a net extraction of fund money while below reserve.
postconditions.possible_false_positive: The 0.01738 ETH figure could reflect a withdrawable value never actually claimed, so a test asserting 'profit' without claiming could overstate real extraction.
postconditions.adversarial_variant: The creator fails to re-list and NO_CURATED/SETTING_UP pauses purchases, or a running keeper collects first; the worst-case test claims the profit and reads the fund strictly lower after the claim.

identity.reason: The actor is the creator using its own listing-set authority; no identity spoof is needed.

quantity.reason: The over-booking equals proceeds*share(m)*k/(n-k); worst case extracts 0.01738 ETH net of fund money.

value_attribution.reason: Fund money (zero-share curated proceeds) is re-attributed to creator profit by a pre-collection listing-set change; the fund ends strictly lower.

authorization.reason: No unauthorized call: the creator is permitted to withdraw/list; the violation is in the accounting, not the gate.

callback.reason: _pullCurated/listNFT target the creator-chosen curated collection and the trusted FWA pool; the leak needs no hostile callback.

timing.reason: The lever requires the game-first window (fund < reserve, draws in flight) and collecting before keeper reconciliation; timing is the trigger.

critical_paths.property: performUpkeep reconciles settled draws and restocks inventory paying the keeper no more than the restock fees it credits (M1/M2), keeps upkeep gas under the keeper floor, and delivers/redeems prizes so each listed prize keeps its own backing (M4) with no over-pay or reentrancy.
critical_paths.attacker_control: A keeper (factory-gated) controls when and how often upkeep runs and can be a contract that re-enters on reward receipt; a winner can be a hostile receiver; ETH can be pushed via receive/depositETH.
critical_paths.asset_authority_ledger: Keeper reward wei must be <= restock fees credited and bounded by MAX_KEEPER_REWARD; prize NFTs/packs leave custody only to their rightful winner or back to the pool on unlist; keeperCredit and profit net to zero over a cycle.
critical_paths.counterexample: A reward-callback reentrancy draining the clamp, a hostile winner bricking reconciliation, or an upkeep paying more than the credited fees; reentrancy is guarded, delivery uses plain transferFrom (no hook), and measured reward never exceeds credited fees.

postconditions.assertion: Non-setup keeper reward <= restock fees credited at 1/3/4.9 gwei over 16 draws each, and the 5-draw burst upkeep uses 2,526,347 gas < the 4,000,000 keeper floor.
postconditions.possible_false_positive: The gas and pay figures are single realised runs at chosen basefees, so a pathological board or basefee between the sampled points could exceed the floor or invert the pay inequality untested.
postconditions.adversarial_variant: A same-block growth larger than the 5-draw burst, or a basefee spike mid-upkeep pushing gas past the floor; the worst-case 5-draw burst and the 1-4.9 gwei sweep bound the measured region only.

postconditions.assertion: The full real-VRF draw cycle delivers the prize to the winner and nets keeperCredit and profit to zero with inventory restored; reward-callback and winner-callback reentrancy attempts are blocked by nonReentrant and plain transferFrom delivery.
postconditions.possible_false_positive: The keeper-reentrancy tests may attempt re-entry on a path the guard already covers while leaving an un-probed re-entry vector (e.g. via a trusted-contract callback) unexercised.
postconditions.adversarial_variant: A hostile winner or reward recipient re-entering performUpkeep/_fillDeficit before the profit clamp settles; the reentrancy suite and the hostile-receiver refund test drive these.

identity.reason: Keeper access is factory-gated (canKeep) and validated in the keeper admin/scope tests; depositETH/receive are permissionless by design and add only backing.

quantity.reason: Keeper reward quantity measured <= credited fees across gas levels and bounded by MAX_KEEPER_REWARD; burst gas measured under the floor.

value_attribution.reason: keeperCredit and profit net to zero over the real cycle; restock fees fund the keeper, not principal.

authorization.reason: Only a gated keeper triggers reconcile/restock; the globalWithdrawOnly and retired checks fail closed.

callback.reason: External calls go to trusted Shapes/Packs/FWA; reward and prize delivery use SafeTransferLib/plain transferFrom, and reentrancy probes are blocked.

timing.reason: The fill gate charges each unreconciled draw the heaviest prize weight and pauses before MAX_BATCH, keeping the in-flight window safe.

critical_paths.property: open() may only enable the pool when balance plus owner proceeds covers requiredReserve, and while the fund is below the reserve claimSurplus/withdrawableSurplus release nothing but true profit, so a creator cannot drain the reserve.
critical_paths.attacker_control: The creator chooses when to open/close and calls claimSurplus with an arbitrary amount and recipient, including repeatedly and while the pool is below reserve after a large prize win.
critical_paths.asset_authority_ledger: The reserve (requiredReserve) must remain backed: withdrawableSurplus == max(0, balance - profit - reserve)-style accounting means while short the creator withdraws 0; close() zeroes keeperCredit and sweeps cleanly.
critical_paths.counterexample: Close, drain, reopen with no reserve (E2), or claim surplus while below reserve to pull backing; open reverts ReserveNotFunded and below-reserve withdrawableSurplus is 0 with profit 0, so no claim reduces the fund below the reserve.

postconditions.assertion: open() reverts unless balance + owner proceeds >= requiredReserve (testOpenRequiresReserve), closing the close-drain-reopen path; the gate runs at open.
postconditions.possible_false_positive: The test funds exactly to the threshold, so an off-by-one or a post-open drift (allowed by design) could pass while a boundary case is mis-handled.
postconditions.adversarial_variant: Opening with proceeds that are counted but not actually withdrawable, or a reserve computed from stale mint fee; requiredReserve reads the live Shapes mint fee and the test exercises the funded/under-funded boundary.

postconditions.assertion: After a targeted 0.5 ETH win tips the fund to 0.6975 < reserve 1.0515 with profit 0, withdrawableSurplus() is 0 and no claim can push balance below the live reserve.
postconditions.possible_false_positive: The single targeted-win scenario reaches one below-reserve state; a different short state (e.g. multiple concurrent shortfalls) could expose a claim path the test did not reach.
postconditions.adversarial_variant: Claiming surplus in a brief window where profit is briefly non-zero while the fund is short; the below-reserve run drove the markup-change timing attack and measured 0 wei moved fund->profit.

identity.reason: open/close/claimSurplus are creator-gated per the authorization matrix.

quantity.reason: withdrawableSurplus is 0 while short; claim amounts above profit revert, measured in the below-reserve run.

value_attribution.reason: Only profit, never reserve/fund backing, is claimable; close zeroes keeperCredit and sweeps to 0.

authorization.reason: Creator-only gates on open/close/claim confirmed in the matrix.

callback.reason: claimSurplus sends ETH via SafeTransferLib to a creator-chosen recipient after profit is decremented (checks-effects-interactions), nonReentrant.

timing.reason: The reserve gate runs at open; post-open drift below reserve is owner-accepted (E1) and the below-reserve regime was driven.

critical_paths.attacker_control: A curated collection whose transfer to the winner reverts forces the failed-delivery branch; the purchaser controls when to call refundFailedDelivery after the 7-day window; the creator controls recoverRefunded timing.
critical_paths.asset_authority_ledger: The NFT returns to the creator and the pool is credited no proceeds (no double-dip, verified); the purchaser's refunded ETH amount is settled inside FWA and was measured as 0 in the blind harness, so where that wei lands is not established here.

postconditions.assertion: recoverRefunded returns the curated NFT to the creator and credits the pool no proceeds (verified); the purchaser's refund ETH amount is FWA-internal and measured 0 in this harness, so the player-side wei destination is NOT established.
postconditions.possible_false_positive: The recovery test asserts the NFT and pool-credit ledger and passes, which could be read as full refund correctness while the purchaser-side refund amount remains unmeasured.
postconditions.adversarial_variant: A failed delivery where FWA refunds the purchaser the wrong amount, or the automatic no-action curated-draw-books-NFT-money case; attributing the player refund needs FWA source (out of blind scope) and the automatic PoC was not built.

identity.reason: refundFailedDelivery is NotPurchaser-gated to the winner and recoverRefunded is creator-gated; identities confirmed in the refund test.

quantity.reason: The pool is credited no proceeds for a failed delivery (no double-dip); the purchaser refund quantity is unmeasured here.
